{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01BZLtom3XdJXD8e1641riY3","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"FastAPI application factory and the module-level app for `uvicorn app_server.main:app`.\"\"\"\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI\n\nfrom app_server import routes\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    \"\"\"Build a new FastAPI application that includes the shared router.\"\"\"\n    application = FastAPI()\n    application.include_router(routes.router)\n    return application\n\n\napp = create_app()\n\"\"\"Shared router registry. Feature stories attach their routes here; static routes go first.\"\"\"\n\nimport datetime\nfrom typing import Annotated\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException, Path\n\nfrom fxrates_app import currencies as currency_service\nfrom fxrates_app import rates as rate_service\nfrom fxrates_app import stats as stats_service\n\nrouter = APIRouter()\nDATE_PATTERN = r\"^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$\"\n\n\n@router.get(\"/health\")\ndef health() -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"Liveness probe. It reaches no store, so it answers even when the database is absent.\"\"\"\n    return {\"status\": \"ok\"}\n\n\n@router.get(\"/stats\")\ndef stats() -> dict[str, int | str | None]:\n    \"\"\"Counts of stored dates and rates, and the first and last publication dates.\"\"\"\n    return stats_service.stats()\n\n\n@router.get(\"/currencies\")\ndef currencies() -> dict[str, str | list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"The base currency and every stored currency code, ascending.\"\"\"\n    return {\"base\": rate_service.BASE, \"currencies\": currency_service.currencies()}\n\n\n@router.get(\"/rates/{date}\")\ndef rates_on_date(date: Annotated[str, Path(pattern=DATE_PATTERN)]) -> dict[str, str | dict[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"The rates of the latest publication on or before `date`; 422 for an impossible date, 404 when none exists.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        requested = datetime.date.fromisoformat(date).isoformat()\n    except ValueError as error:\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail=f\"not a real calendar date: {date}\") from error\n    found = rate_service.rates_on(requested)\n    if found is None:\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f\"no publication on or before {requested}\")\n    effective, rates = found\n    return {\"date\": effective, \"requested\": requested, \"base\": rate_service.BASE, \"rates\": rates}\n\"\"\"In-process test client for the application; used by acceptance and the pytest suite.\"\"\"\n\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app_server.main import create_app\n\n\ndef web_client() -> TestClient:\n    \"\"\"Return a TestClient wrapping a new application instance.\"\"\"\n    return TestClient(create_app())\n----\n\"\"\"Rates on a calendar day: the effective publication date and the rates published on it.\n\nThe ECB publishes on working days only, so a request for any date resolves to the latest\npublication on or before it. Rates are returned as the stored text, never converted to a float.\nReads go through `db.rates` only.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom persistence import Database\n\nfrom fxrates_app.config import open_store\n\nBASE = \"EUR\"\n\n\ndef _effective(db: Database, day: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the latest stored publication date on or before `day`, or None when none exists.\"\"\"\n    rows = db.rates.list_on_or_before(as_of=day)\n    return rows[0].date if rows else None\n\n\ndef effective_date(d: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the latest publication date on or before `d`, or None when no such date exists.\"\"\"\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        return _effective(db, d)\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n\n\ndef rates_on(requested: str) -> tuple[str, dict[str, str]] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return (effective date, {currency: stored rate text}) for `requested`, or None.\n\n    None means no publication exists on or before `requested`. The base currency never appears in\n    the mapping.\n    \"\"\"\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        effective = _effective(db, requested)\n        if effective is None:\n            return None\n        rows = db.rates.list_for_date(date=effective)\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n    return effective, {row.currency: row.rate for row in rows if row.currency != BASE}\n\"\"\"Summary of the store: how many dates and rates it holds, and its first and last publication dates.\n\nEvery value is derived from `db.rates.list_all_keys`; the service counts and takes the extremes.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fxrates_app.config import open_store\n\n\ndef stats() -> dict[str, int | str | None]:\n    \"\"\"Return the dates and rates counts and the first and last dates, None when nothing is stored.\"\"\"\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        keys = db.rates.list_all_keys()\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n    dates = sorted({key.date for key in keys})\n    return {\n        \"dates\": len(dates),\n        \"rates\": len(keys),\n        \"first\": dates[0] if dates else None,\n        \"last\": dates[-1] if dates else None,\n    }\n----\n\"\"\"ECB history archive download: the single function in the application that opens a network connection.\n\n`download_archive` returns the bytes of the ECB history zip. The fetch command calls it through this\nmodule attribute, so a test replaces this one seam and never reaches the network.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport urllib.request\n\nECB_ARCHIVE_URL = \"https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/eurofxref/eurofxref-hist.zip\"\nTIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30.0\n\n\ndef download_archive(url: str) -> bytes:\n    \"\"\"Return the bytes served at `url`. A transport failure or timeout raises OSError.\"\"\"\n    with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=TIMEOUT_SECONDS) as response:\n        return response.read()\n\"\"\"Database location: one place decides which store the application opens.\n\nResolution order: DATABASE_URL, then DATABASE_PATH, then data/app.db. The environment is read at\ncall time. Application code opens the store only through `persistence.open_database`.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\n\nfrom persistence import Database, open_database\n\nDEFAULT_DATABASE_PATH = \"data/app.db\"\nSQLITE_PREFIX = \"sqlite://\"\n\n\ndef database_path() -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return the database location from the environment, falling back to data/app.db.\"\"\"\n    url = os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_URL\", \"\")\n    if url.startswith(SQLITE_PREFIX):\n        url = url[len(SQLITE_PREFIX):]\n    if url:\n        return url\n    path = os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_PATH\", \"\")\n    if path:\n        return path\n    return DEFAULT_DATABASE_PATH\n\n\ndef open_store() -> Database:\n    \"\"\"Open the store named by `database_path()` through the persistence library.\"\"\"\n    return open_database(database_path())","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"5565c188-00ff-47a2-9fda-b6e435524dad","uuid":"8d89774d-e876-45e4-b375-2a2715563dcb","timestamp":"2026-10-27T16:31:01.225Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"\"\"\"FastAPI application factory and the module-level app for `uvicorn app_server.main:app`.\"\"\"\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI\n\nfrom app_server import routes\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    \"\"\"Build a new FastAPI application that includes the shared router.\"\"\"\n    application = FastAPI()\n    application.include_router(routes.router)\n    return application\n\n\napp = create_app()\n\"\"\"Shared router registry. Feature stories attach their routes here; static routes go first.\"\"\"\n\nimport datetime\nfrom typing import Annotated\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException, Path\n\nfrom fxrates_app import currencies as currency_service\nfrom fxrates_app import rates as rate_service\nfrom fxrates_app import stats as stats_service\n\nrouter = APIRouter()\nDATE_PATTERN = r\"^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$\"\n\n\n@router.get(\"/health\")\ndef health() -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"Liveness probe. It reaches no store, so it answers even when the database is absent.\"\"\"\n    return {\"status\": \"ok\"}\n\n\n@router.get(\"/stats\")\ndef stats() -> dict[str, int | str | None]:\n    \"\"\"Counts of stored dates and rates, and the first and last publication dates.\"\"\"\n    return stats_service.stats()\n\n\n@router.get(\"/currencies\")\ndef currencies() -> dict[str, str | list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"The base currency and every stored currency code, ascending.\"\"\"\n    return {\"base\": rate_service.BASE, \"currencies\": currency_service.currencies()}\n\n\n@router.get(\"/rates/{date}\")\ndef rates_on_date(date: Annotated[str, Path(pattern=DATE_PATTERN)]) -> dict[str, str | dict[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"The rates of the latest publication on or before `date`; 422 for an impossible date, 404 when none exists.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        requested = datetime.date.fromisoformat(date).isoformat()\n    except ValueError as error:\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail=f\"not a real calendar date: {date}\") from error\n    found = rate_service.rates_on(requested)\n    if found is None:\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f\"no publication on or before {requested}\")\n    effective, rates = found\n    return {\"date\": effective, \"requested\": requested, \"base\": rate_service.BASE, \"rates\": rates}\n\"\"\"In-process test client for the application; used by acceptance and the pytest suite.\"\"\"\n\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app_server.main import create_app\n\n\ndef web_client() -> TestClient:\n    \"\"\"Return a TestClient wrapping a new application instance.\"\"\"\n    return TestClient(create_app())\n----\n\"\"\"Rates on a calendar day: the effective publication date and the rates published on it.\n\nThe ECB publishes on working days only, so a request for any date resolves to the latest\npublication on or before it. Rates are returned as the stored text, never converted to a float.\nReads go through `db.rates` only.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom persistence import Database\n\nfrom fxrates_app.config import open_store\n\nBASE = \"EUR\"\n\n\ndef _effective(db: Database, day: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the latest stored publication date on or before `day`, or None when none exists.\"\"\"\n    rows = db.rates.list_on_or_before(as_of=day)\n    return rows[0].date if rows else None\n\n\ndef effective_date(d: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the latest publication date on or before `d`, or None when no such date exists.\"\"\"\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        return _effective(db, d)\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n\n\ndef rates_on(requested: str) -> tuple[str, dict[str, str]] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return (effective date, {currency: stored rate text}) for `requested`, or None.\n\n    None means no publication exists on or before `requested`. The base currency never appears in\n    the mapping.\n    \"\"\"\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        effective = _effective(db, requested)\n        if effective is None:\n            return None\n        rows = db.rates.list_for_date(date=effective)\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n    return effective, {row.currency: row.rate for row in rows if row.currency != BASE}\n\"\"\"Summary of the store: how many dates and rates it holds, and its first and last publication dates.\n\nEvery value is derived from `db.rates.list_all_keys`; the service counts and takes the extremes.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fxrates_app.config import open_store\n\n\ndef stats() -> dict[str, int | str | None]:\n    \"\"\"Return the dates and rates counts and the first and last dates, None when nothing is stored.\"\"\"\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        keys = db.rates.list_all_keys()\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n    dates = sorted({key.date for key in keys})\n    return {\n        \"dates\": len(dates),\n        \"rates\": len(keys),\n        \"first\": dates[0] if dates else None,\n        \"last\": dates[-1] if dates else None,\n    }\n----\n\"\"\"ECB history archive download: the single function in the application that opens a network connection.\n\n`download_archive` returns the bytes of the ECB history zip. The fetch command calls it through this\nmodule attribute, so a test replaces this one seam and never reaches the network.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport urllib.request\n\nECB_ARCHIVE_URL = \"https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/eurofxref/eurofxref-hist.zip\"\nTIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30.0\n\n\ndef download_archive(url: str) -> bytes:\n    \"\"\"Return the bytes served at `url`. A transport failure or timeout raises OSError.\"\"\"\n    with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=TIMEOUT_SECONDS) as response:\n        return response.read()\n\"\"\"Database location: one place decides which store the application opens.\n\nResolution order: DATABASE_URL, then DATABASE_PATH, then data/app.db. The environment is read at\ncall time. Application code opens the store only through `persistence.open_database`.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\n\nfrom persistence import Database, open_database\n\nDEFAULT_DATABASE_PATH = \"data/app.db\"\nSQLITE_PREFIX = \"sqlite://\"\n\n\ndef database_path() -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return the database location from the environment, falling back to data/app.db.\"\"\"\n    url = os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_URL\", \"\")\n    if url.startswith(SQLITE_PREFIX):\n        url = url[len(SQLITE_PREFIX):]\n    if url:\n        return url\n    path = os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_PATH\", \"\")\n    if path:\n        return path\n    return DEFAULT_DATABASE_PATH\n\n\ndef open_store() -> Database:\n    \"\"\"Open the store named by `database_path()` through the persistence library.\"\"\"\n    return open_database(database_path())","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01BZLtom3XdJXD8e1641riY3","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01NzCjYFcZKsdHRmuLwkCHQy","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"The `load` command: validate an ECB history file, store its rates, report the counts.\n\n`parse_history` checks the whole file before the first write, so a rejected file exits 3 and stores\nnothing. A file that cannot be opened or decoded exits 1 before any parsing or store access. Each rate is then written through the declared `rates.replace_rate` operation, which\nreplaces a rate already stored for the same date and currency, so loading a file twice leaves the\ndatabase unchanged.\n\nThe persistence library exposes no transaction operation, so each replace commits on its own. The\nvalidation above is what keeps a rejected file from changing anything; a store failure part way\nthrough a valid file is not rolled back.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sys\n\nfrom cli.dispatcher import register_command\nfrom cli.help import print_help\nfrom fxrates_app.config import open_store\nfrom fxrates_app.ecb import RejectedFile, parse_history\n\nOPERATIONAL_FAILURE = 1\nREJECTED = 3\nHELP_FLAG = \"--help\"\n\n\ndef load(rest: list[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Load the file named in `rest[0]` and return the exit code. The argument list is pre-validated.\"\"\"\n    if rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return print_help(\"load\")\n    try:\n        with open(rest[0], encoding=\"utf-8\", newline=\"\") as handle:\n            text = handle.read()\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as error:\n        print(f\"error: cannot read {rest[0]}: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return OPERATIONAL_FAILURE\n    try:\n        rates = parse_history(text)\n    except RejectedFile as error:\n        print(f\"error: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return REJECTED\n\n    return store_and_report(rates)\n\n\ndef store_and_report(rates: list[tuple[str, str, str]]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Store validated (date, currency, rate_text) rows and print the dates and rates counts.\n\n    Shared by `load` and `fetch`, so both commands store and report the same way.\n    \"\"\"\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        for date, currency, rate in rates:\n            db.rates.replace_rate(date=date, currency=currency, rate=rate)\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n\n    dates = {date for date, _, _ in rates}\n    print(\"dates,rates\")\n    print(f\"{len(dates)},{len(rates)}\")\n    return 0\n\n\nregister_command(\"load\", load)\n\"\"\"Command registry and dispatch.\n\nCommand stories register a handler under a command name at import time. `main` hands the\nremaining arguments to the handler and returns the handler's exit code.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sys\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom cli import usage\n\nUSAGE_ERROR = 2\n\n_handlers: dict[str, Callable[[list[str]], int]] = {}\n\n\ndef register_command(name: str, handler: Callable[[list[str]], int]) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Map a command name to its handler; registering a name again replaces the handler.\"\"\"\n    _handlers[name] = handler\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Validate `argv`, dispatch `argv[0]` to its registered handler, and return the exit code.\"\"\"\n    args = list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)\n    try:\n        usage.validate(args, _handlers)\n    except usage.UsageError as exc:\n        print(f\"error: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return USAGE_ERROR\n    handler = _handlers.get(args[0])\n    if handler is None:\n        print(f\"error: command not available in this build: {args[0]}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return USAGE_ERROR\n    return handler(args[1:])\n\"\"\"The `serve` command: run the HTTP API in the foreground on 127.0.0.1 until SIGTERM or SIGINT.\n\nThe port is validated by `cli.usage` before dispatch. Before uvicorn binds, this command probes the\nport, so a port already in use exits 1 with one stderr line and answers no requests. Uvicorn's own\nsignal capture is replaced: it re-raises a captured SIGTERM after shutdown, which would end the\nprocess by signal instead of with exit 0. Here the signal only asks the server to stop.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport contextlib\nimport signal\nimport socket\nimport sys\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterator\nfrom types import FrameType\n\nimport uvicorn\n\nfrom cli.dispatcher import register_command\nfrom cli.help import print_help\n\nHOST = \"127.0.0.1\"\nDEFAULT_PORT = 8000\nAPP_PATH = \"app_server.main:app\"\nOPERATIONAL_FAILURE = 1\nHELP_FLAG = \"--help\"\nPORT_FLAG = \"--port\"\nSTOP_SIGNALS = (signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIGINT)\n\n\nclass _ForegroundServer(uvicorn.Server):\n    \"\"\"Uvicorn server that leaves signal handling to `serve`.\"\"\"\n\n    @contextlib.contextmanager\n    def capture_signals(self) -> Iterator[None]:\n        yield\n\n\ndef _port_is_free(port: int) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Bind the port the way uvicorn does, then release it. True when nothing else holds it.\"\"\"\n    probe = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)\n    try:\n        probe.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)\n        probe.bind((HOST, port))\n    except OSError:\n        return False\n    finally:\n        probe.close()\n    return True\n\n\ndef _requested_port(rest: list[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the port named by `--port <n>`, or the default when no option is given.\"\"\"\n    return int(rest[1]) if rest else DEFAULT_PORT\n\n\ndef _stop_on(server: uvicorn.Server) -> Callable[[int, FrameType | None], None]:\n    def handle(_signum: int, _frame: FrameType | None) -> None:\n        server.should_exit = True\n\n    return handle\n\n\ndef serve(rest: list[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Serve the application until a stop signal; It performs no database access and reads no file.\nRates keep their published text; they are never converted to a number.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport datetime\nimport io\nimport re\nfrom decimal import Decimal\n\nFIRST_HEADER_FIELD = \"Date\"\nNOT_AVAILABLE = \"N/A\"\n\n_DATE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}\")\n_CURRENCY_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[A-Z]{3}\")\n_RATE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?\")\n\n\nclass RejectedFile(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Raised when an ECB history file violates the format; no rate from it may be written.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef parse_history(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Validate the whole file and return (date, currency, rate_text) for every non-N/A value.\n\n    Raises RejectedFile on the first violation found anywhere in the file.\n    \"\"\"\n    rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(text)))\n    if not rows:\n        raise RejectedFile(\"file has no header\")\n\n    header = _drop_trailing_comma(rows[0])\n    if not header or header[0] != FIRST_HEADER_FIELD:\n        raise RejectedFile(\"header must begin with Date\")\n    currencies = header[1:]\n    for code in currencies:\n        if not _CURRENCY_PATTERN.fullmatch(code):\n            raise RejectedFile(f\"malformed currency code in header: {code!r}\")\n    if len(set(currencies)) != len(currencies):\n        raise RejectedFile(\"currency code repeated in header\")\n\n    rates: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []\n    seen_dates: set[str] = set()\n    for line_number, raw in enumerate(rows[1:], start=2):\n        fields = _drop_trailing_comma(raw)\n        if len(fields) != len(header):\n            raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has {len(fields)} fields, expected {len(header)}\")\n\n        date_text = fields[0]\n        _check_date(date_text, line_number)\n        if date_text in seen_dates:\n            raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} repeats date {date_text}\")\n        seen_dates.add(date_text)\n\n        for code, value in zip(currencies, fields[1:]):\n            if value == NOT_AVAILABLE:\n                continue\n            _check_rate(value, line_number)\n            rates.append((date_text, code, value))\n\n    return rates\n\n\ndef _drop_trailing_comma(fields: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The ECB writes a trailing comma on each line; the resulting empty last field is ignored.\"\"\"\n    if fields and fields[-1] == \"\":\n        return fields[:-1]\n    return fields\n\n\ndef _check_date(text: str, line_number: int) -> None:\n    if not _DATE_PATTERN.fullmatch(text):\n        raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has a malformed date: {text!r}\")\n    try:\n        datetime.date.fromisoformat(text)\n    except ValueError as error:\n        raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has an impossible date: {text!r}\") from error\n\n\ndef _check_rate(text: str, line_number: int) -> None:\n    if not _RATE_PATTERN.fullmatch(text):\n        raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has a malformed rate: {text!r}\")\n    if Decimal(text) == 0:\n        raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has a zero rate: {text!r}\")","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"5565c188-00ff-47a2-9fda-b6e435524dad","uuid":"4f918662-b693-4f07-83bf-a395227ffdc2","timestamp":"2026-10-27T16:31:02.180Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"\"\"\"The `load` command: validate an ECB history file, store its rates, report the counts.\n\n`parse_history` checks the whole file before the first write, so a rejected file exits 3 and stores\nnothing. The argument list is pre-validated.\"\"\"\n    if rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return print_help(\"load\")\n    try:\n        with open(rest[0], encoding=\"utf-8\", newline=\"\") as handle:\n            text = handle.read()\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as error:\n        print(f\"error: cannot read {rest[0]}: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return OPERATIONAL_FAILURE\n    try:\n        rates = parse_history(text)\n    except RejectedFile as error:\n        print(f\"error: {error}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return REJECTED\n\n    return store_and_report(rates)\n\n\ndef store_and_report(rates: list[tuple[str, str, str]]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Store validated (date, currency, rate_text) rows and print the dates and rates counts.\n\n    Shared by `load` and `fetch`, so both commands store and report the same way.\n    \"\"\"\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        for date, currency, rate in rates:\n            db.rates.replace_rate(date=date, currency=currency, rate=rate)\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n\n    dates = {date for date, _, _ in rates}\n    print(\"dates,rates\")\n    print(f\"{len(dates)},{len(rates)}\")\n    return 0\n\n\nregister_command(\"load\", load)\n\"\"\"Command registry and dispatch.\n\nCommand stories register a handler under a command name at import time. `main` hands the\nremaining arguments to the handler and returns the handler's exit code.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sys\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom cli import usage\n\nUSAGE_ERROR = 2\n\n_handlers: dict[str, Callable[[list[str]], int]] = {}\n\n\ndef register_command(name: str, handler: Callable[[list[str]], int]) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Map a command name to its handler; Output is captured\n# in full so the exit status of pytest is kept (a pipe would hide it).\nset +e\n\"$PROJECT_DIR/.venv/bin/pytest\" -q >\"$LOG_FILE.pytest\" 2>&1\nSTATUS=$?\nset -e\ncat \"$LOG_FILE.pytest\" | tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\"\nrm -f \"$LOG_FILE.pytest\"\n\necho \"=== $SCRIPT_NAME finished at $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') with status $STATUS ===\" | tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\"\nexit \"$STATUS\"\n\"\"\"ECB history file validation: one pure function checks a whole file before any write.\n\n`parse_history` reads the text of an ECB euro reference rate history file and returns every\nnon-N/A value as (date, currency, rate_text). It performs no database access and reads no file.\nRates keep their published text; they are never converted to a number.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport datetime\nimport io\nimport re\nfrom decimal import Decimal\n\nFIRST_HEADER_FIELD = \"Date\"\nNOT_AVAILABLE = \"N/A\"\n\n_DATE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}\")\n_CURRENCY_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[A-Z]{3}\")\n_RATE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?\")\n\n\nclass RejectedFile(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Raised when an ECB history file violates the format; no rate from it may be written.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef parse_history(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Validate the whole file and return (date, currency, rate_text) for every non-N/A value.\n\n    Raises RejectedFile on the first violation found anywhere in the file.\n    \"\"\"\n    rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(text)))\n    if not rows:\n        raise RejectedFile(\"file has no header\")\n\n    header = _drop_trailing_comma(rows[0])\n    if not header or header[0] != FIRST_HEADER_FIELD:\n        raise RejectedFile(\"header must begin with Date\")\n    currencies = header[1:]\n    for code in currencies:\n        if not _CURRENCY_PATTERN.fullmatch(code):\n            raise RejectedFile(f\"malformed currency code in header: {code!r}\")\n    if len(set(currencies)) != len(currencies):\n        raise RejectedFile(\"currency code repeated in header\")\n\n    rates: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []\n    seen_dates: set[str] = set()\n    for line_number, raw in enumerate(rows[1:], start=2):\n        fields = _drop_trailing_comma(raw)\n        if len(fields) != len(header):\n            raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has {len(fields)} fields, expected {len(header)}\")\n\n        date_text = fields[0]\n        _check_date(date_text, line_number)\n        if date_text in seen_dates:\n            raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} repeats date {date_text}\")\n        seen_dates.add(date_text)\n\n        for code, value in zip(currencies, fields[1:]):\n            if value == NOT_AVAILABLE:\n                continue\n            _check_rate(value, line_number)\n            rates.append((date_text, code, value))\n\n    return rates\n\n\ndef _drop_trailing_comma(fields: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The ECB writes a trailing comma on each line; the resulting empty last field is ignored.\"\"\"\n    if fields and fields[-1] == \"\":\n        return fields[:-1]\n    return fields\n\n\ndef _check_date(text: str, line_number: int) -> None:\n    if not _DATE_PATTERN.fullmatch(text):\n        raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has a malformed date: {text!r}\")\n    try:\n        datetime.date.fromisoformat(text)\n    except ValueError as error:\n        raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has an impossible date: {text!r}\") from error\n\n\ndef _check_rate(text: str, line_number: int) -> None:\n    if not _RATE_PATTERN.fullmatch(text):\n        raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has a malformed rate: {text!r}\")\n    if Decimal(text) == 0:\n        raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has a zero rate: {text!r}\")","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01NzCjYFcZKsdHRmuLwkCHQy","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01UEohQ3pAkd7NJ3jqHtkMP5","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"SQLite engine for ``db.py``.\n\nShipped by Drydock and copied into the build unchanged. Do not edit it here.\n\nSQLite is the development and test engine. It parses the same declaration PostgreSQL does and\nignores what it does not enforce — ``VARCHAR(n)`` length in particular — so one rendered schema\nserves both engines and nothing is stripped for one of them.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\nimport threading\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any\n\ntry:\n    from .db import Driver\nexcept ImportError:  # flat layout\n    from db import Driver\n\n__all__ = [\"SqliteDriver\"]\n\n\nclass SqliteDriver(Driver):\n    \"\"\"One connection per thread, opened on first use in that thread.\n\n    A ``sqlite3.Connection`` belongs to the thread that created it and raises ``ProgrammingError``\n    when used from another, so a single connection opened during construction is valid in no web\n    request at all. This is not concurrency: queries stay sequential within a workflow, and the\n    rule only stops one connection being shared across unrelated ones.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    paramstyle = \"qmark\"\n    returning = False\n\n    def __init__(self, dsn: str) -> None:\n        self._path = _path_from(dsn)\n        self._local = threading.local()\n        self._pinned: sqlite3.Connection | None = None\n\n    def connect(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:\n        if self._pinned is not None:\n            return self._pinned\n        connection = getattr(self._local, \"connection\", None)\n        if connection is None:\n            connection = self._open()\n            self._local.connection = connection\n        return connection\n\n    def pin(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:\n        # Shared across threads on purpose; ``Database`` serializes every operation on it.\n        if self._pinned is None:\n            self._pinned = self._open(check_same_thread=False)\n        return self._pinned\n\n    def identity(self) -> str:\n        return self._path if self._path == \":memory:\" else str(Path(self._path).resolve())\n\n    def _open(self, *, check_same_thread: bool = True) -> sqlite3.Connection:\n        if self._path != \":memory:\":\n            Path(self._path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n        # Autocommit by default; an explicit BEGIN suspends it until ROLLBACK.\n        connection = sqlite3.connect(\n            self._path, isolation_level=None, check_same_thread=check_same_thread\n        )\n        connection.execute(\"PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL\")\n        connection.execute(\"PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON\")\n        return connection\n\n    def close(self) -> None:\n        if self._pinned is not None:\n            self._pinned.close()\n            self._pinned = None\n            return\n        connection = getattr(self._local, \"connection\", None)\n        if connection is not None:\n            connection.close()\n            self._local.connection = None\n\n    def inserted_key(self, cursor: Any) -> Any:\n        return cursor.lastrowid\n\n\ndef _path_from(dsn: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Read a filesystem path out of a DSN, accepting a bare path as well as a URL.\"\"\"\n    if \"://\" not in dsn:\n        return dsn or \":memory:\"\n    _, _, remainder = dsn.partition(\"://\")\n    return remainder or \":memory:\"\n----\n\nclass Database:\n    \"\"\"One store, presented to callers as declared tables with declared methods.\n\n    Callers construct one instance, share it freely, and call methods synchronously. Connection\n    handling is internal and may change without affecting any caller.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, dsn: str, schema: Schema, *, driver: Driver | None = None) -> None:\n        self._rollback_owner = None\n        self._schema = schema\n        driver = driver if driver is not None else open_driver(dsn)\n        self._harness = _harness\n        self._driver = self._harness.join(driver) if self._harness is not None else driver\n        grouped = schema.by_table()\n        for table in schema.tables:\n            setattr(self, table.name, TableAccess(table, grouped.get(table.name, ()), self))\n\n    @property\n    def driver(self) -> Driver:\n        if self._harness is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"driver access is forbidden inside the acceptance transaction\")\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"driver access is forbidden inside a rollback session\")\n        return self._driver\n\n    def close(self) -> None:\n        if self._harness is not None:\n            return  # the acceptance harness owns the shared connection\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"the rollback session owns connection lifetime\")\n        self._driver.close()\n\n    @contextmanager\n    def rollback_session(self):\n        \"\"\"Use this connection for setup, behavior and assertions; always roll back.\n        })\n\n\ndef statements(sql: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Split a DDL script into statements.\n\n    Comment lines are dropped and a semicolon inside a quoted literal does not end a statement —\n    a ``DEFAULT \\'a;b\\'`` would otherwise be cut in half, and the halves are not valid SQL.\n    \"\"\"\n    body = \"\\n\".join(line for line in sql.splitlines() if not line.lstrip().startswith(\"--\"))\n    parts: list[str] = []\n    current: list[str] = []\n    quoted = False\n    for character in body:\n        if character == \"'\":\n            quoted = not quoted\n        if character == \";\" and not quoted:\n            parts.append(\"\".join(current))\n            current = []\n            continue\n        current.append(character)\n    parts.append(\"\".join(current))\n    return [statement.strip() for statement in parts if statement.strip()]\n\n\ndef open_driver(dsn: str) -> Driver:\n    \"\"\"Select the engine from the DSN, so one build serves SQLite in test and Postgres in production.\"\"\"\n    scheme = dsn.split(\"://\", 1)[0].lower() if \"://\" in dsn else \"sqlite\"\n    if scheme in (\"postgres\", \"postgresql\"):\n        try:\n            from .postgres import PostgresDriver\n        except ImportError:  # flat layout\n            from postgres import PostgresDriver\n\n        return PostgresDriver(dsn)\n    if scheme in (\"sqlite\", \"file\") or \"://\" not in dsn:\n        try:\n            from .sqlite import SqliteDriver\n        except ImportError:  # flat layout\n            from sqlite import SqliteDriver\n\n        return SqliteDriver(dsn)\n    raise PersistenceError(\n        f\"no persistence driver for {scheme!r}. Drydock ships sqlite and postgres; add a driver \"\n        \"beside this file and a branch here for another engine.\"\n    )\n----\n        table='rates',\n        verb='list',\n        inputs=('since',),\n        row=RatesListCurrenciesOutput,\n        columns=('currency',),\n        match=(),\n        name='list_currencies',\n        compare=(('since', '>=', 'date'),),\n        order=(('currency', 'asc'),),\n    ),\n    Operation(\n        identifier='FEATURE-RATE-006',\n        table='rates',\n        verb='list',\n        inputs=('currency', 'start_date', 'end_date'),\n        row=RatesListCurrencyHistoryOutput,\n        columns=('date', 'currency', 'rate'),\n        match=(),\n        name='list_currency_history',\n        compare=(('start_date', '>=', 'date'), ('end_date', '<=', 'date')),\n        order=(('date', 'asc'),),\n    ),\n    Operation(\n        identifier='FEATURE-RATE-007',\n        table='rates',\n        verb='delete',\n        inputs=('from_date',),\n        row=None,\n        columns=(),\n        match=('from_date',),\n        name='delete_from_date',\n        compare=(('from_date', '>=', 'date'),),\n    ),\n    ),\n)\n\n\ndef open_database(dsn: str) -> Database:\n    \"\"\"Open the declared store. The base currency never appears in\n    the mapping.\n    \"\"\"\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        effective = _effective(db, requested)\n        if effective is None:\n            return None\n        rows = db.rates.list_for_date(date=effective)\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n    return effective, {row.currency: row.rate for row in rows if row.currency != BASE}","newString":"def _rates_of(db: Database, effective: str) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"Return {currency: stored rate text} for the publication on `effective`, base excluded.\"\"\"\n    rows = db.rates.list_for_date(date=effective)\n    return {row.currency: row.rate for row in rows if row.currency != BASE}\n\n\ndef rates_on(requested: str) -> tuple[str, dict[str, str]] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return (effective date, {currency: stored rate text}) for `requested`, or None.\n\n    None means no publication exists on or before `requested`. The base currency never appears in\n    the mapping.\n    \"\"\"\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        effective = _effective(db, requested)\n        if effective is None:\n            return None\n        rates = _rates_of(db, effective)\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n    return effective, rates\n\n\ndef latest_rates() -> tuple[str, dict[str, str]] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return (latest publication date, {currency: stored rate text}), or None when nothing is stored.\n\n    The latest date is the first row of `list_on_or_before` called without a bound.\n    \"\"\"\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        rows = db.rates.list_on_or_before()\n        if not rows:\n            return None\n        effective = rows[0].date\n        rates = _rates_of(db, effective)\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n    return effective, rates","originalFile":"\"\"\"Rates on a calendar day: the effective publication date and the rates published on it.\n\nThe ECB publishes on working days only, so a request for any date resolves to the latest\npublication on or before it. Rates are returned as the stored text, never converted to a float.\nReads go through `db.rates` only.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom persistence import Database\n\nfrom fxrates_app.config import open_store\n\nBASE = \"EUR\"\n\n\ndef _effective(db: Database, day: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the latest stored publication date on or before `day`, or None when none exists.\"\"\"\n    rows = db.rates.list_on_or_before(as_of=day)\n    return rows[0].date if rows else None\n\n\ndef effective_date(d: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the latest publication date on or before `d`, or None when no such date exists.\"\"\"\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        return _effective(db, d)\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n\n\ndef rates_on(requested: str) -> tuple[str, dict[str, str]] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return (effective date, {currency: stored rate text}) for `requested`, or None.\n\n    None means no publication exists on or before `requested`. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CgT4bE8mgeTDNdqwt9JF8","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01A1esBrM3ohQzGEsbEa5KHg","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/FxRates/runs/20261027.152427/build/FxRates/tests/test_load_visibility.py","content":"\"\"\"Load visibility: a completed load is seen by the next API request; a rejected load changes nothing.\n\nThe command and the web client share one acceptance transaction, so a rate the command writes is\nread back by the next request through the same store. Each test empties the store first and rolls\nback at the end.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nfrom collections.abc import Iterator\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\nfrom persistence import db as persistence_db\nfrom persistence.testing import db_session\n\n\n@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)\ndef rolled_back_transaction() -> Iterator[None]:\n    \"\"\"Share one connection between the command, the route and the test, then roll everything back.\"\"\"\n    persistence_db.begin_acceptance_transaction()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        persistence_db.end_acceptance_transaction()\n\n\ndef write_history(path: Path, header: list[str], rows: list[list[str]]) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Write a file the way the ECB does: every line ends with a trailing comma.\"\"\"\n    buf = io.StringIO()\n    writer = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator=\"\\n\")\n    writer.writerow(header + [\"\"])\n    for row in rows:\n        writer.writerow(row + [\"\"])\n    path.write_text(buf.getvalue(), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    return path\n\n\ndef empty_store(db) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Remove every stored rate inside the acceptance transaction.\"\"\"\n    db.rates.delete_from_date(from_date=\"0000-01-01\")\n\n\ndef test_completed_load_is_visible_to_the_next_stats_request(web_client, tmp_path: Path) -> None:\n    d = \"1900-12-30\"\n    path = write_history(tmp_path / \"load.csv\", [\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[d, \"1.5\", \"2.25\"]])\n    with db_session() as db:\n        empty_store(db)\n        before = web_client.get(\"/stats\").json()\n\n        code, out, err = cli_runner(\"load\", str(path))\n        after = web_client.get(\"/stats\").json()\n\n    assert code == 0\n    assert after == {\"dates\": 1, \"rates\": 2, \"first\": d, \"last\": d}\n    assert after[\"dates\"] == before[\"dates\"] + 1\n    assert after[\"rates\"] == before[\"rates\"] + 2\n    assert after[\"last\"] == d\n\n\ndef test_completed_load_is_visible_to_the_next_latest_request(web_client, tmp_path: Path) -> None:\n    d = \"1900-12-31\"\n    path = write_history(tmp_path / \"latest.csv\", [\"Date\", \"ZZA\"], [[d, \"3.5\"]])\n    with db_session() as db:\n        empty_store(db)\n\n        code, _, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", str(path))\n        response = web_client.get(\"/rates/latest\")\n\n    assert code == 0\n    assert response.status_code == 200\n    assert response.json()[\"date\"] == d\n    assert response.json()[\"rates\"] == {\"ZZA\": \"3.5\"}\n\n\ndef test_rejected_load_leaves_stats_unchanged(web_client, tmp_path: Path) -> None:\n    good = \"1900-11-01\"\n    bad = \"1900-11-02\"\n    path = write_history(\n        tmp_path / \"bad.csv\",\n        [\"Date\", \"ZZA\"],\n        [[bad, \"1.5\"], [good, \"1.5x\"]],\n    )\n    with db_session() as db:\n        empty_store(db)\n        db.rates.replace_rate(date=\"1900-10-30\", currency=\"ZZA\", rate=\"1\")\n        before = web_client.get(\"/stats\").json()\n\n        code, out, err = cli_runner(\"load\", str(path))\n        after = web_client.get(\"/stats\").json()\n        written = db.rates.list_for_date(date=bad)\n\n    assert code == 3\n    assert out == \"\"\n    assert after == before\n    assert written == []\n\n\ndef visibility: a completed load is seen by the next API request; a rejected load changes nothing.\n\nThe command and the web client share one acceptance transaction, so a rate the command writes is\nread back by the next request through the same store. Each test empties the store first and rolls\nback at the end.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nfrom collections.abc import Iterator\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\nfrom persistence import db as persistence_db\nfrom persistence.testing import db_session\n\n\n@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)\ndef rolled_back_transaction() -> Iterator[None]:\n    \"\"\"Share one connection between the command, the route and the test, then roll everything back.\"\"\"\n    persistence_db.begin_acceptance_transaction()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        persistence_db.end_acceptance_transaction()\n\n\ndef write_history(path: Path, header: list[str], rows: list[list[str]]) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Write a file the way the ECB does: every line ends with a trailing comma.\"\"\"\n    buf = io.StringIO()\n    writer = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator=\"\\n\")\n    writer.writerow(header + [\"\"])\n    for row in rows:\n        writer.writerow(row + [\"\"])\n    path.write_text(buf.getvalue(), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    return path\n\n\ndef empty_store(db) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Remove every stored rate inside the acceptance transaction.\"\"\"\n    db.rates.delete_from_date(from_date=\"0000-01-01\")\n\n\ndef test_completed_load_is_visible_to_the_next_stats_request(web_client, tmp_path: Path) -> None:\n    d = \"1900-12-30\"\n    path = write_history(tmp_path / \"load.csv\", [\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[d, \"1.5\", \"2.25\"]])\n    with db_session() as db:\n        empty_store(db)\n        before = web_client.get(\"/stats\").json()\n\n        code, out, err = cli_runner(\"load\", str(path))\n        after = web_client.get(\"/stats\").json()\n\n    assert code == 0\n    assert after == {\"dates\": 1, \"rates\": 2, \"first\": d, \"last\": d}\n    assert after[\"dates\"] == before[\"dates\"] + 1\n    assert after[\"rates\"] == before[\"rates\"] + 2\n    assert after[\"last\"] == d\n\n\ndef test_completed_load_is_visible_to_the_next_latest_request(web_client, tmp_path: Path) -> None:\n    d = cli_runner(\"load\", str(path))\n        response = web_client.get(\"/rates/latest\")\n\n    assert code == 0\n    assert response.status_code == 200\n    assert response.json()[\"date\"] == d\n    assert response.json()[\"rates\"] == {\"ZZA\": \"3.5\"}\n\n\ndef test_rejected_load_leaves_stats_unchanged(web_client, tmp_path: Path) -> None:\n    good = \"1900-11-01\"\n    bad = \"1900-11-02\"\n    path = write_history(\n        tmp_path / \"bad.csv\",\n        [\"Date\", \"ZZA\"],\n        [[bad, \"1.5\"], [good, \"1.5x\"]],\n    )\n    with db_session() as db:\n        empty_store(db)\n        db.rates.replace_rate(date=\"1900-10-30\", currency=\"ZZA\", rate=\"1\")\n        before = web_client.get(\"/stats\").json()\n\n        code, out, err = cli_runner(\"load\", str(path))\n        after = web_client.get(\"/stats\").json()\n        written = db.rates.list_for_date(date=bad)\n\n    assert code == 3\n    assert out == \"\"\n    assert after == before\n    assert written == []\n\n\ndef test_loading_the_same_file_twice_leaves_stats_unchanged(web_client, tmp_path: Path) -> None:\n    path = write_history(tmp_path / \"again.csv\", [\"Date\", \"ZZA\"], [[\"1900-10-07\", \"7.5\"]])\n str(path))[0] == 0\n        second = web_client.get(\"/stats\").json()\n\n    assert second == first\n"}}}
